description: Verify LED-off-after-reset, button-press toggling (including debounce and fast response), and Serial1 ON/OFF reporting for the debounced button toggle lab.

steps.requirement: LED (D13) is off immediately after reset, with no spurious toggles.
First button press turns the LED on (exactly one toggle).
On turning the LED on, the board prints 'ON' on Serial1.
Second button press turns the LED back off (exactly one toggle).
On turning the LED off, the board prints 'OFF' on Serial1.
The LED reacts quickly to a press (within 20 ms), so a user perceives no delay.
A single bouncy press toggles the LED exactly once, regardless of contact bounce.

assumptions: The handout gives no numeric bound for 'reacts quickly / no noticeable delay', so a 20 ms maximum button-to-LED delay is assumed.
A 100 ms press width is used to simulate a clean (non-bouncy) button press/release.
Bounce stimulus uses 5 bounces at 200 microsecond intervals (the rig's example bouncy-press pattern) ending at the pressed (low) level.
A 200-300 ms observation window is assumed sufficient to capture the LED's response and any associated UART message after each stimulus.
D13 (timer_capture capable) is used with logic_trace to detect LED toggle edges and final level, since logic_trace only requires digital edge sensing.

not_graded.requirement: Debouncing must be implemented in software without blocking delay() calls.
not_graded.reason: Implementation technique (blocking vs. non-blocking code) cannot be verified by electrical measurement alone.
Code style/comments are not observable through electrical measurement.
